title: Obscured star formation in bright z ≃ 7 Lyman-break galaxies
question: How much obscured star formation is there in bright z~7 LBGs, what does the IRX-beta relation look like, and does dust shape the bright end of the UV luminosity function?

data.angular_resolution: 1.1 x 1.4 arcsec (natural weighting); 1.4 x 1.7 arcsec with 1 arcsec taper

what.value: HST/WFC3 JH140 imaging and M_UV, UV SFRs

evidence.quote: High-resolution rest-frame UV imaging of the sample is available from *HST*/Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3) as described in (cite: Bowler2016).

what.value: Greybody beta = 1.6 from local infrared luminous galaxies

evidence.quote: We fix the exponent to $\beta = 1.6$, which is the best-fitting value from the sample of local infrared luminous galaxies presented in (cite: Casey2012).

recipe.method: Natural-weighted tclean continuum; peak flux within 1 arcsec of HST centroid; Gaussian fit for total flux for detection and stacks; 2sigma upper limits as peak+2xRMS
Stack at UltraVISTA Ks centroids, all six and excluding ID65666
Modified blackbody with 1.3 mm flux, CMB correction, integrated 8-1000 um
assumptions: optically thin; CMB contrast correction following DaCunha2013

recipe.goal: SED fitting for photo-z and stellar mass
recipe.method: LePhare with BC03 models, exponentially declining SFH, Chabrier IMF, 1/5 Zsun, Calzetti dust, 16 bands

recipe.goal: Measure UV slope beta and IRX
recipe.method: Power-law fit to photometry at 1270-2580 A; Y band excluded for three highest-z galaxies; IRX = L_FIR/L_UV
Compare ALMA and HST centroids for ID65666; blind source extraction of serendipitous sources and cross-match to HST to test astrometry; positional accuracy 0.6xFWHM/SNR
FIR SFR from Kennicutt2012 and UV SFR from Madau1998, both with Chabrier IMF

evidence.quote: with a measured peak flux of $124 \pm 24\,\mu{\rm Jy}$ or $5.2\sigma$ significance
results in a total flux of $168 \pm 56\,\mu\,{\rm Jy}$
We therefore find that the offset has a significance of $\simeq 4\sigma$ in the absence of systematic errors
The measured FIR emission from our sample implies an average UV attenuation of $A_{\rm UV} \simeq 0.5$–$1.0\,$mag

answer_key.quantity: Obscured fraction of SFR in ID65666

evidence.quote: with $75$% of the total SFR being obscured (increasing to $85$% in the case of T$\,= 50\,$K)

not_stated_but_needed: CASA tclean parameters (cell size, image size, niter, deconvolver)
Gaussian fitting task/method for total flux
Pipeline continuum channel selection / line flagging
missing_for_reproduction: Photometric catalogue and HST imaging from Bowler2016 needed
score_reason: Archival data and key steps are described, but imaging/stacking parameters are missing and the UV photometry comes from other papers.
rediscovery_reason: Data are an ALMA Cycle 3 project; the recipe (natural-weight imaging, flux measurement, greybody L_FIR) is mostly specified and results are numeric.
